Both arms Texture border, --runs 10, one requester, device_label read out of each result.json. JUDGED ON stale_px FROM docs/testing/border_swatch_origin.py, NOT on differing pixels: the count swings 40x on an unchanged binary (0 0 0 0 146 181 1847 2352 2430 5640) because each swatch has a fixed cost if it loses and a run's total is the sum over whichever subset lost, so 146 and 5,640 are the same event once and three times. At the moment it resumes, draw N is already inside the segment just published, so ANY un-consumed pushbuffer leaves draw N's read still to come while surface N+1 is being written. No intermediate bound is sufficient. The measurement agrees from the other side: the guest is at most ONE iteration ahead (successor explains 100%, successor+2 explains 32/146, 400/992, 234/591), so the skew to remove is exactly one submission's worth and nothing less will do.
